transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me. It’ll sound like it’s coming through the conference room walls, or from my phone even when it’s turned off. Usually it’s board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company. It’s so clear sometimes that I answer them out loud, and then I realize no one else heard anything.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get stressed and on edge, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had days where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that.
Do you believe these people are actually talking about you and trying to harm your reputation?
I don’t know. When it’s happening, it feels real, like they are talking about me. But I’m not sure what’s actually going on or whether they’re really trying to damage me.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been upset and worn down, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It’s been about three months, I think. The voices—like from the walls or sometimes my phone—started around then.
Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do things you usually would do?

Yes. I used to be the one pushing ideas forward and calling people after openings, staying on top of everything. Now I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at the agenda and not really do anything. I barely talk to my husband or my staff, and I don’t feel much about work anymore, even though I used to love it.
Before the voices started, had you already begun withdrawing from people or losing motivation?

Yes, I think that had started already. I used to be the one pushing things forward, calling people, keeping everything moving. But then I started just sitting at my desk, staring at the agenda and not doing much. I wasn’t talking much to my husband or my staff either. Work just felt... empty, even though I used to really care about it.
Before these voices began, had you recently had a medical illness or injury?
No, not that I can think of. I don’t remember being sick or having an injury before it started.
During this period, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I felt sad most of the day every day. It was more like I felt flat or empty, like I didn’t have much feeling about things.
Have you had the feeling that other people can hear your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve worried about what people think of me, but I haven’t really had the feeling that they can hear my thoughts without me saying them.
Have other people told you that your speech has become hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
I’m not sure. No one has really said that to me directly, at least not in those words. I haven’t noticed myself jumping around, but I guess I might not always catch it.
Have you had times when your behavior felt very disorganized or strange to other people?

Yes. There have been times like that. In meetings, or at gallery events, I’ll suddenly stand up and start rearranging pens or name cards into patterns. Sometimes I repeat something someone just said, or I’ll hold my hands up like I’m presenting something, but I’m not really presenting anything. Afterward I can see it didn’t make sense for the situation, and I know it probably looked strange.
Before these past three months, had you noticed any other changes like withdrawing from people, losing motivation, or acting oddly for several months?

Yes. Before this got really noticeable, I had already been pulling back for months. I used to be the one pushing ideas and calling everyone after openings, and now I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at the agenda. I barely talk to my husband or my staff some days. And the strange part is I don’t feel much about the work anymore, even though I used to really love it.
From when those changes like pulling back, losing motivation, or acting oddly first began, has it been at least six months in total by now?

Yes. It’s definitely been more than six months. I’d say it started building about two years and four months ago, around when the company expanded and I was put in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division.
